references.text: God predicts that the water from the Nile will turn to blood on dry land, which is fulfilled here in 7:20
The Lord gives instructions to Moses to strike the water of the Nile with his staff to turn it into blood
The psalmist recalls how God turned the rivers and streams of Egypt into blood
The psalmist reminds us that God turned Egypt's waters into blood and killed the fish
God refers to His power to turn the sea into a desert and cause the fish to die, echoing the plague in Egypt
In Revelation, a third of the sea is turned into blood, recalling the plague of blood in Egypt
The two witnesses have power to turn water into blood, like Moses and Aaron in Egypt
The third angel pours out his bowl on the rivers and springs, and they become blood
Both verses document the first signs at Pharaoh's court where the staff is used to carry out God's judgment against Egypt.
Thematic parallel between the first plagues where Aaron uses the staff to bring God's judgment upon Egypt.
Thematic connection among the plagues where Moses uses the staff to bring natural disasters upon Egypt.
Direct reference back to the event in 7:20 where the staff is used to strike the Nile.
